## Reading
MechanicLens — repair estimate
Document: estimate
Reading: Standard 1 · Check 1 · Question this 4

*(No personal identifiers appeared in this paste, so nothing to redact.)*

## Anatomy
| Line | Plain-English name | What it claims to cover | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Parts — front brake pads | New ceramic friction pads for the front brakes | 129.00 |
| 2 | Parts — front brake rotors | Two replacement front brake discs | 218.00 |
| 3 | Maintenance service — brake fluid flush | Replacing the brake fluid; price is not broken into fluid vs. labor | 89.00 |
| 4 | Labor — front pad and rotor replacement | 1.5 hours at 145.00/hr to install lines 1–2 | 217.50 |
| 5 | Fee — shop supplies | Consumables/materials; contents and basis not stated | 12.50 |
| 6 | Tax — sales tax at 7.25% | Tax on the 666.00 subtotal | 48.29 |
| | **Total** | | **714.29** |

Arithmetic check: 129.00 + 218.00 + 89.00 + 217.50 + 12.50 = 666.00; 7.25% of 666.00 = 48.29. The total adds up.

## Scope check
**Does not match.** The stated symptom is "a rattle from the back of the car when I go over bumps." Every work line in this estimate addresses the **front** brakes (lines 1, 2, 4) or routine fluid maintenance (line 3). Nothing in the estimate references the rear of the vehicle, and no diagnostic or inspection line appears that would show how the front-brake work was connected to the rattle. This mismatch is the finding, and the labels below inherit it — the off-symptom lines are labeled on that basis.

## Labels
| Line | Label | Reason (quoted) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Question this** | "Front brake pad set, ceramic" — quoted work does not match the stated symptom ("rattle from the back of the car… over bumps"); nothing references the rear of the car |
| 2 | **Question this** | "Front brake rotors, pair" — same scope basis; front rotors do not correspond to a rear-of-car complaint |
| 3 | **Question this** | "Brake fluid flush" — maintenance item not connected to the stated symptom; bundled into a quote that does not address the complaint |
| 4 | **Question this** | "Labor — replace front pads and rotors, 1.5 hr @ 145.00/hr" — hours and rate are stated, but the operation itself does not address the symptom |
| 5 | **Check** | "Shop supplies" — a flat fee with no contents or basis stated |
| 6 | **Standard** | "Sales tax 7.25%" — rate is stated and the arithmetic verifies |

## Questions to ask
1. "My complaint was a rattle from the back when I go over bumps. Which line in this estimate addresses that?" — a good answer sounds like: pointing to a specific inspection finding, ideally written on the estimate, that explains the connection.
2. "Was the source of the rattle inspected? What did you find, and can that be noted on the estimate?" — a good answer sounds like: describing where they looked and what they found, or offering an inspection step before any parts are replaced.
3. "Is the brake fluid flush related to the rattle, or is it routine maintenance I can decide on separately?" — a good answer sounds like: a plain statement of which it is, and whether declining it affects anything else on the estimate.
4. "What brand and part number are the pads and rotors — OEM or aftermarket?" — a good answer sounds like: naming the brand and line without hedging.
5. "What does the 12.50 shop supplies charge cover?" — a good answer sounds like: stating the basis (a posted percentage or per-job rate) or showing the posted fee schedule.

## Decision
The kit stops here — what you sign is your call. Before you decide: photograph this estimate; note anything promised at the counter and who said it; keep the paperwork chain (estimate → signed authorization → final invoice) so the invoice can be compared line-by-line against what you agreed to. The authorization line is present but blank — fill in the date and only what was actually agreed. No verdict is given here.

## Needs confirmation
- [CONFIRM: whether an inspection for the rattle was performed or offered — no diagnostic line appears on the estimate]
- [NOT SHOWN: part numbers for the pads and rotors]
- [NOT SHOWN: whether the pads/rotors are OEM or aftermarket]
- [NOT SHOWN: estimate validity or expiration date]
- [NOT SHOWN: basis for the 12.50 shop supplies fee]
